summary: Give managed VMs an emulated TPM 2.0 (BUG-0196), an explicit Secure Boot choice instead of libvirt's silent pick (BUG-0199), a second CD drive for a driver disc addressed by libvirt user alias (BUG-0198), and Windows-aware clock and Hyper-V defaults (BUG-0210); ship swtpm on Nex Core and remove per-VM TPM state on delete. API impact: changed contract — protocol.VMBoot.SecureBoot/TPM, protocol.VMCreateSpec.DriversMediaID, protocol.VMMediaRequest.Drive and protocol.DriversDriveCapability, carried by vm-create, vm-update and vm-media.

guide.reason: Three new operator-visible choices on the Create VM wizard's Boot and media page and on Edit: Secure Boot, TPM and Driver disc. create-virtual-machine.md states the Windows 11 prerequisites (UEFI, Secure Boot, TPM 2.0, swtpm on the host), documents each control with its actual labels, records that the driver disc is never in the boot order, and adds troubleshooting for a host without swtpm, for the virtio-win Load driver step and for Setup's unexplained requirements message. It also states that Guest operating system = Windows now changes devices (localtime RTC and Hyper-V enlightenments) instead of being a hint only. edit-virtual-machine.md documents the stopped-only Secure Boot and TPM fields, the compatibility reading for a UEFI VM created before they existed, the BitLocker caution, how a VM that predates the second CD drive gains it, and the Windows clock change. Both pages state plainly that none of this was walked through on a lab host: there is none in this lane, so the new behaviour is covered by unit tests over the generated libvirt definition only.

api.reason: API impact: changed contract. Three additive fields and one capability, all already defined in internal/protocol and implemented here on the Core side. (1) protocol.VMBoot gains secure_boot ("" | "on" | "off") and tpm ("" | "none" | "2.0"), carried by the vm-create and vm-update agent commands and by POST/PUT /api/v1/vms. Compatibility is the load-bearing part: "" means Secure Boot on with the Microsoft keys enrolled, because that is the firmware libvirt already selected for every UEFI VM defined before the field existed, so an older definition re-sent unchanged keeps the firmware its guest was installed against; "" tpm means no TPM, so no existing VM gains a device. protocol.NeedsStop lists both as stop-required, and protocol.ValidateVMSpec refuses secure_boot=on without UEFI and any tpm value other than 2.0/none. (2) protocol.VMCreateSpec gains drivers_media_id, the ISO in the VM's second CD drive, refused when equal to media_id. (3) protocol.VMMediaRequest gains drive ("" | "install" | "drivers"); "" is the install drive, which is what every Controller sent before, and protocol.ApplyVMMedia records an insert or eject into media_id or drivers_media_id accordingly. validateManaged refuses an unknown drive before anything is issued. (4) protocol.DriversDriveCapability ("vm-media-drivers-drive-v1") is reported by the agent's v2 capability list; a Controller must not send drive="drivers" to a host without it. Drive identification on the host is the ua-nex-cdrom-install and ua-nex-cdrom-drivers libvirt user aliases; a domain defined by an older Core carries neither and its single cdrom is always the install drive. Errors are host-reported task failures naming the missing host support (no swtpm, no tpm-crb model, no emulated backend, no driver disc drive while running). Retry safety is unchanged: a vm-media request is still resolved against the domain libvirt actually holds, so a re-sent request converges.

roadmap.reason: Defect fixes against findings W1, W3, W4 and W15 of the Windows 11 UEFI lab report. No milestone, acceptance gate or delivery order changes; Windows 11 was already an intended guest.

state.reason: Durable record: the pool master's managed journal under the agent state directory (internal/vmhost ManagedEngine, one JSON entry per operation). secure_boot, tpm and drivers_media_id are fields of protocol.VMCreateSpec, so they are written by the vm-create or vm-update entry that set them and read back as the VM's current definition by managedCurrent/currentDefinitions; a vm-media request on either drive is recorded into the same entry by recordVMMedia through protocol.ApplyVMMedia. The libvirt target letters of the two CD drives are host-side placement, journalled as media_target and drivers_target, and re-derived by managedCurrent for an entry written before the second drive existed so adding it renames no device the guest has. Adoption: a fresh Controller learns all of it from the host's inventory report, which reports each VM's current definition from that journal (ManagedEngine.Applied), exactly as it already learns the VM's name, disks and install media. Nothing here is stored in the Controller database, and a Controller that is deleted and rebuilt recovers every value from the pool master without an operator re-entering anything. swtpm's own TPM state is not Nex's: it lives under /var/lib/libvirt/swtpm/<uuid> on the host that runs the VM, created by libvirt on first start. deleteVM asks virsh undefine to remove it with --tpm (and the UEFI variable store with --nvram), deciding both from every journaled revision through vmEverHad rather than the current one, because firmware and the TPM are editable and an edit that drops either leaves its state behind.
state.record: Pool master's Nex Core managed journal (protocol.VMCreateSpec.Boot.SecureBoot, Boot.TPM and DriversMediaID on the VM's current vm-create/vm-update entry; media_target and drivers_target beside them). Host-side TPM state is swtpm's /var/lib/libvirt/swtpm/<uuid>.
state.adoption: The host reports each VM's current definition in its inventory (ManagedEngine.Applied); a re-enrolling host restores Secure Boot, TPM and driver disc with the VM, with no Controller-side copy.

verification.method: Ran and inspected, all output read rather than assumed: `go build ./...` (exit 0, no output); `go test -race ./internal/vmhost/ ./internal/protocol/` (ok nex.local/nex/internal/vmhost 12.801s; ok nex.local/nex/internal/protocol); `go vet ./internal/vmhost/` (clean); `gofmt -l internal/vmhost/firmware.go internal/vmhost/firmware_test.go internal/vmhost/managed.go` (clean). New focused tests in internal/vmhost/firmware_test.go, each run and passing: TestManagedDomainXMLTPM (tpm-crb + emulator 2.0 present only when asked for, and no <tpm> element at all otherwise); TestManagedDomainXMLSecureBoot (the unset/on/off cases, that enrolled-keys follows secure-boot, that SMM is present exactly when Secure Boot is on, and that BIOS gets no firmware features); TestManagedDomainXMLWindowsDefaults (localtime clock and relaxed/vapic/spinlocks retries=8191 for Windows, and that linux/other/"" produce no <clock> and no hyperv); TestManagedDomainXMLTwoCDDrives (both drives, their user aliases, distinct SATA targets, both read-only, the driver disc with no boot order, an empty drivers drive still present, and a definition that reuses one target or omits the drivers target refused); TestCDROMDriveResolution (alias resolution in either document order, the older single-unaliased-cdrom domain resolving to the install drive with no drivers drive, a libvirt-assigned alias not hiding the install drive); TestDriversTargetAvoidsExistingDevices (placement past an existing SATA disk, and managedCurrent backfilling an older journal entry to sdb without renaming vda/sda); TestManagedDeleteRemovesTPMState (undefine carries --tpm exactly when the VM has one, and --nvram is not lost); TestManagedCapacityRefusesTPMWithoutSwtpm (six domcapabilities shapes: accepted with the emulator backend, refused naming swtpm when the backend, the device or the whole section is absent, refused naming tpm-crb and version 2.0 where those are missing, and the same host still accepting a VM with no TPM); TestValidateManagedDefinitionFirmwareAndTPM (a host that dropped the TPM and a host that inverted secure-boot are both refused, and libvirt omitting the features is tolerated); TestManagedMediaDriversDrive (an insert reaching the drivers tray by alias and recording into drivers_media_id while media_id and media_boot_order are untouched, an eject clearing only that record, an install-drive request still reaching the install tray, an older domain refusing a drivers insert while running with a message naming the reason, a stopped insert attaching a tray that carries the drivers alias, and an unknown drive refused); TestApplyLiveAddsDriversDriveToOlderDomain (a running VM defined by an older Core gets the second drive added config-only, never --live or --persistent, with no media change issued). Regression value was demonstrated, not assumed: in a scratch copy of the package outside the repository, each fix was reverted in turn and the matching test observed failing — removing the <tpm> device failed TestManagedDomainXMLTPM ("TPM presence false, want true") and TestValidateManagedDefinitionFirmwareAndTPM ("a silently missing TPM must be refused"); restoring the bare firmware='efi' failed TestManagedDomainXMLSecureBoot on all three cases ("UEFI definition must state its firmware features"); removing the Windows defaults failed TestManagedDomainXMLWindowsDefaults ("a Windows guest keeps local time in the RTC"); removing the second drive failed TestManagedDomainXMLTwoCDDrives ("both CD drives must exist") and TestApplyLiveAddsDriversDriveToOlderDomain; ignoring the requested drive failed TestManagedMediaDriversDrive with the driver disc landing on sda, the install tray; dropping --tpm failed TestManagedDeleteRemovesTPMState ("undefine --tpm present=false"); dropping the preflight failed five TestManagedCapacityRefusesTPMWithoutSwtpm cases. The scratch copy was deleted afterwards and the repository tree was not modified by it. Pre-existing vmhost tests were kept passing, including TestManagedDeleteRetainsOrWipesDisks (asserts undefine --nvram is still issued for a VM without a TPM) and the whole managed/media/defaults/update suites. Installer: the package assertions installer/check.sh makes over installer/packages.txt were replayed in python3 and all passed (no duplicate, required set present, every name plain); python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_storage_packaging.py' (Ran 14 tests, OK). NOT DONE, and not claimed: there is no lab host in this lane, so nothing below the Go layer was executed. No libvirt accepted the generated XML, no VM was defined, started or installed, no swtpm process ran, no ISO was built and no installer ran, so the <firmware> feature form, the tpm-crb emulator device, undefine --tpm, the second SATA cdrom, the Hyper-V enlightenments and the localtime clock are verified as the definition Nex produces and the virsh arguments it issues, not as behaviour observed on a host. The compatibility claim that an existing UEFI VM keeps booting is tested at the definition level (SecureBoot "" produces secure-boot=yes, enrolled-keys=yes and SMM on, which is what libvirt had selected) and has not been proved by booting an installed guest. Deliberately not added: the vpindex, synic, stimer, reset, frequencies and tlbflush enlightenments and the rtc/pit/hpet/hypervclock timers, because each asks KVM for a capability a host or a nested hypervisor can lack and none could be verified here; the three emitted are the set libvirt and virt-install have defaulted to for Windows. Known and unverified: the second CD drive takes one more port on q35's single AHCI controller, whose usual limit is six SATA devices, so the number of SATA disks a VM can carry before libvirt runs out of ports drops by one. That ceiling was already reachable (the specification allows eight disks on any bus) and no additional SATA controller is declared here, because the behaviour could not be observed on a host; it is reported as an open item rather than guessed at. scripts/check_docs.py was deliberately not run in this lane; concurrent unfinished work in the tree makes its worktree result unreadable, and the primary runs it for the batch. Post-review additions, run and inspected after the coordination changes landed: the cdrom alias names are declared once for the package (cdromInstallAlias/cdromDriversAlias, shared with observeGuest in guest.go) rather than duplicated; the undefine flags moved from the current revision to vmEverHad over every journaled revision, with TestManagedDeleteRemovesStateAnEditDroppedLater in internal/vmhost/delete_test.go covering create-with-TPM / edit-away / delete, create-UEFI / edit-to-BIOS / delete, and a VM that never had either. That test is load-bearing: restoring the current-revision form in a scratch copy failed two of its three subtests ("must carry --tpm" and "must carry --nvram": state the edit dropped would survive deletion). Final state on the real tree: go build ./... exit 0; go vet ./internal/vmhost/ exit 0; gofmt -l over all seven changed Go files, clean; go test -race -count=1 ./internal/vmhost/ ./internal/protocol/ both ok; go test -count=1 ./... ok across all eleven packages. OPEN, and not closed by this change: the journal-decided --tpm is a strict improvement but on a reading of libvirt's source (qemuExtDevicesCleanupHost iterates the persistent definition's def->tpms) it removes state only for TPM devices the domain still carries, so once an edit has redefined the domain without <tpm> the flag has nothing to iterate and /var/lib/libvirt/swtpm/<uuid> survives regardless. That is source reading, not libvirt's documented contract, and was not observed on a host; it is reported to the primary as its own defect rather than treated as fixed here.
